result.topic_en: Euler explains that two projections of a space curve determine it, and sets up the problem of finding a space curve maximizing or minimizing an integral of V dx, introducing notation p, q, r and p', q', r' for the derivatives of y and z.

items.quote: Sufficit autem ad curvam determinandam duas tantum projectiones priores nosse, quandoquidem his tertia projectio jam determinatur.
items.english: It suffices, however, for determining the curve to know only the first two projections, since by these the third projection is already determined.

items.quote: Quodsi jam ejusmodi curva desideretur, in qua formula integralis $\int V\partial x$ maximum minimumve obtineat valorem, ubi V sit functio quaecunque non solum ipsarum trium variabilium $x$, $y$ et $z$, sed etiam earum differentialia cujuscunque ordinis involvat, ac fortasse etiam novas formulas integrales complectatur
items.english: Suppose now a curve is sought in which the integral formula ∫V dx attains a maximum or minimum value, where V is any function involving not only the three variables x, y and z but also their differentials of any order, and perhaps also containing further integral formulas.

items.quote: ad hoc expediendum duae aequationes sunt necessariae, ex quibus tam valorem ipsius $y$, quam ipsius $z$, per $x$ definire liceat
items.english: To accomplish this, two equations are necessary, from which the value both of y and of z can be defined in terms of x.

items.quote: statuamus primo pro variabili $y$, ejusque differentialibus, $\partial y = p\partial x$, $\partial p = q\partial x$, $\partial q = r\partial x$ etc.
items.english: Let us first set, for the variable y and its differentials, dy = p dx, dp = q dx, dq = r dx, etc.
